unit.title: Landforms, Earth and Space Exploration
unit.about_unit: Examines human adaptations to diverse landforms (mountains, deserts, coasts) and expands student horizons to orbital spaceflight and viewing the Earth from space.

facilitation_guide.headline: Ecological Stewardship

chapter.title: Landforms and Life
chapter.tagline: Living across mountains, desert sands, fertile plains, and mangrove coasts
chapter.overview: India's topography varies from rugged Himalayan ridges and arid Thar sands to lush Gangetic plains and coastal deltas. Students investigate how local terrain dictates architectural styles (slanted slate roofs, thick mud insulation, stilt dwellings), terrace farming, and daily human livelihoods.

sections.title: India's Geographic Panoramas: Diverse Terrains
sections.subtitle: Comparing mountains, plateaus, plains, deserts, and coasts

storyNarrative.dialogue: Our country has high snow mountains in the north, broad river plains in the center, a rocky triangular plateau, a golden desert in the west, and two long ocean coastlines!

concept.heading: Major Physiographic Divisions
concept.keyRule: Himalayan Mountains, Northern Plains, Peninsular Plateau, Indian Desert, Coastal Plains, and Islands.

sections.title: Mountain Living & Terrace Agriculture
sections.subtitle: Carving steps on steep mountain slopes to prevent soil erosion

storyNarrative.dialogue: On our steep Himalayan slopes, rain would wash all soil away! So we carve flat step terraces. Water stays in each step, letting our apples, barley, and potatoes flourish!

concept.heading: Terrace Cultivation (Step Farming)
concept.keyRule: Carving horizontal terraces slows rainwater runoff, conserves precious topsoil, and creates arable plots on mountain slopes.

questions.prompt: Why do farmers in mountainous regions practice step (terrace) farming?
options: To make the hill look pretty
To prevent soil erosion and retain moisture on steep slopes
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent soil erosion and retain moisture on steep slopes
questions.hint: Step contours stop rapid rainwater runoff.

sections.title: Desert & Coastal Adaptations: Mud Walls & Mangroves
sections.subtitle: Thick mud thermal buffers and mangrove tsunami shields

storyNarrative.dialogue: In Rajasthan our mud walls are two feet thick with thatched roofs of thorny bushes—they keep our rooms cool during scorching 48°C afternoons!

concept.heading: Thermal Inertia & Coastal Bio-Shields
concept.keyRule: Thick earthen walls delay solar heat transfer. Along coastlines, dense mangrove roots bind tidal soil and buffer storms.
